title: Collision Dynamics of Topologically Pumped Solitons
authors: Ning Mao, Guang-Can Guo, Xi-Wang Luo
abstract: Soliton pumping enables controlled transport of localized wave packets through the interplay between nonlinearity and band topology. Interactions between such wave packets provide an additional means to manipulate their localization and subsequent motion. Here, we investigate collisions of solitons in a driven bichromatic lattice, where solitons associated with bands of opposite Chern numbers are pumped toward one another. For intracomponent collisions, the soliton that dominates the collision survives as a localized outgoing wave packet, while the weaker one can lose its distinct localized identity. For intercomponent collisions, attractive interaction produces spatial locking, whereas repulsive interaction induces redistribution toward the lowest band and reverses the motion of the initially excited-band wave packet. Remarkably, for collisions between vector solitons with comparable initial intensities, the difference between their internal relative phases controls the collision outcome, favoring capture for in-phase preparation and re-separation for out-of-phase preparation. These results connect nonlinear scattering with subsequent topological pumping and identify initial intensity, intercomponent interaction, and relative phase as control parameters for manipulating localized transport within the same pumping protocol.
summary: This paper explores how the collision dynamics of solitons are manipulated when the underlying system undergoes topological pumping. By analyzing single-component, intercomponent, and vector soliton collisions, the authors demonstrate that the final state—whether capture or re-separation—is dictated by precise control parameters like initial intensity imbalance and relative phase. This highlights the rich interplay between nonlinearity, topology, and quantum control in wave systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex dynamics of soliton collisions when the system is subjected to topological pumping mechanisms.
main_result: The collision outcome is highly controllable by initial conditions, specifically the relative initial intensities, the sign of the intercomponent interaction, and the internal relative phase for vector solitons.
method: The study relies on numerical simulations of coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations, employing advanced diagnostics like core tracking, energy ratio analysis, and overlap energy calculations.
model_or_system: The model involves solitons in a driven bichromatic lattice, described by coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations, exhibiting topological pumping linked to Chern numbers.
key_observables: Post-collision displacement (Q_out), core separation D(t), energy ratio eta(t), and overlap energy E_ol(D, Δθ).
important_parameters: Initial relative intensities, intercomponent interaction strength (attractive vs. repulsive), and the internal relative phase (Δθ) for vector solitons.
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes approximations such as treating cores as rigid wave packets for kinetic energy estimation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate linear band spectra with Chern numbers, density evolution for different collision types (intra/inter), and phase-dependent collision outcomes for vector solitons.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the context of topological pumping to analyzing single-component collisions, then detailing intercomponent interactions based on attraction/repulsion, and finally focusing on the phase control in vector soliton collisions.
why_interesting: This work bridges nonlinear wave physics (solitons) with topological concepts (Chern numbers) in a controlled, tunable manner, offering new control knobs (phase, interaction strength) for wave transport.
